_comment: Pack sizes that B2BWave modelled as separate products, expressed as Solidus
variants of one product instead. Keyed by b2b_product_id, like
product_overrides.json, but kept in its own file because this is a structural
change rather than a field correction.
'keep' is the product that survives and becomes the page customers land on.
'variants' are listed in display order, so the FIRST entry is the default the
storefront preselects -- the operator wants the larger pack default everywhere.
'slug' is set explicitly rather than regenerated from the name: friendly_id
keeps the slug it first generated, so a renamed product would otherwise keep a
URL naming a product that no longer exists under that name.
'supersedes' lists the b2b_product_ids folded into it; those products are
discontinued rather than deleted, because order history references them.
Their master SKUs are cleared as part of folding them in. Solidus enforces SKU
uniqueness across every variant that is not soft-deleted (Spree::Variant
#enforce_unique_sku?), so the superseded product cannot keep the SKU that the
new variant now claims. The original is recorded in 'was_sku' so nothing is
lost, and the product keeps its name and history in the admin.
Applied by Nsb::ProductConsolidator via bin/rails nsb:catalog:consolidate.
